sources.citation: Armstrong, Robert G. 1983. The Idomoid languages of the Benue and Cross River valleys. Journal of West African Languages 13(1): 91-149. Sec. 3.1.1 'Kyana or Eastern Alago' (pp. 125-131, reproducing D.R. Longley's 1970 field notes from Obi) and 3.1.2 'Idoma Nokwu or Western Alago'.

sources.note: Nothing. The Alago sections give tone facts only (p.126: 'Alago nouns cannot begin with a mid-tone (though verbs may). In general, an initial mid-tone on an Idoma noun becomes high-tone in Alago.'), segmental correspondences, palatalization, a five-vowel system and phoneme charts (p.130); the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the article.
